materials.content_note: AIQ Opening Bell, Vol 6, Issue 8, August 1997. Interview by David Vomund. Holy Grail buy rules (sells reversed): 1. The 14-period ADX must initially be greater than 30 and rising. 2. Look for a retracement in price to the 20-period exponential moving average, usually accompanied by a turndown in ADX. 3. When price touches the 20-period moving average, put a buy stop above the high of the previous bar. 4. Once filled, enter a protective sell stop at the newly formed swing low. Trail stops as profits grow. Also: 'The worst thing you can do in terms of market timing is to buy in the middle of a trading range. Either buy new highs, or buy pullbacks...'; 'Moves often start in either direction with an impulse and a thrust. It may be a range expansion, an increase in standard deviation, a breakaway gap, or even a failure to make a lower low'; stop process ('Most often, I'll get out if the market fails to do what I thought it would do'); failure example Eaton Corp ('no reason to be in this trade'). The interview references the Holy Grail pattern from the Raschke & Connors book 'Street Smarts'; the pattern lineage is shared with Larry Connors, not independent confirmation.
materials.content_type: official interview (Linda Bradford Raschke; patterns: Holy Grail, Three-Day Unfilled Gap Reversal, Wolfe Wave; timing; stops)
materials.diversity_role: PRIMARY material for the Holy Grail 4-step buy rules; no-trade (middle of range); impulse/thrust cue list; stop process; failure example (Eaton Corp); lineage reference to the Raschke & Connors 'Street Smarts' book

materials.canonical_title: The Discerning Trader: Linda Bradford Raschke
materials.content_note: Stocks & Commodities V.11:9 (360-366), 1993, interview by Thom Hartle. Raschke's own stated pullback framework: 'If there is a trend, I'll try to always look for buying a pullback to a moving average... I personally use a 20-period exponential moving average on all my markets.' ADX no-trade/fade rules: 'I avoid the markets where the ADX falls below 20 and is declining... I will not fade a market... where the ADX is above 32 and rising.' Prior-day high/low as reference points. This material supplies the 20-period EMA usage statement and the ADX-based no-trade constraints for the Holy Grail family.
materials.content_type: official interview (Thom Hartle; pullback to 20-period EMA; ADX no-trade rules; prior-day levels)
materials.diversity_role: Raschke's own stated pullback-in-trend framework: 'If there is a trend, I'll try to always look for buying a pullback to a moving average... I personally use a 20-period exponential moving average on all my markets'; ADX no-trade/fade rules (ADX<20 declining avoid; ADX>32 rising do not fade)

materials.canonical_title: Trading Style and Daily Market Regimen
materials.content_note: Active Trader, February 2004, interview by Mark Etzkorn (a day with Linda Raschke, Nov 2003). Used for NO_TRADE / FAILURE_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE context for the Holy Grail family: 'If I try to guess a breakout, I'm wrong 90 percent of the time. I'm a perfect contrary indicator. ... I just know if it's a low ADX, I'm going to be wrong if I try to guess.' Also: 'In a down-trending market, an early gap up is a short 95 percent of the time.' These are no-trade / failure constraints, not entry rules for the Holy Grail pullback.
materials.content_type: official interview (Mark Etzkorn; trend days; no-trade; failure context)
materials.diversity_role: no-trade / failure context for the Holy Grail family: 'If I try to guess a breakout, I'm wrong 90 percent of the time' (guess-breakout failure, low-ADX warning)

materials.content_note: Active Trader, August 2000, interview by Mark Etzkorn. Used for EXIT_TRIGGER / PROFIT_TARGET / POST_ENTRY_INVALIDATION management context for the Holy Grail family: 'The minute the market gives back more than it should, you get out on the first reaction or pause'; 'If the market reaches a price objective, and you're really not sure if it's going to continue, you have to at least take half the position off'; 'Ninety percent of what I do is price-based. Indicators are just derivatives of price.' These are qualitative management principles; no numeric exit is pinned.
materials.content_type: official interview (Mark Etzkorn; management/exit; price-based emphasis)
materials.diversity_role: management/exit principles for held positions: give-back exit on first reaction/pause; take at least half off at a price objective when continuation uncertain; price-based emphasis ('Ninety percent of what I do is price-based')

materials.content_note: Active Trader, March 2004, interview by Mark Etzkorn (follow-up). PRIMARY material for the Holy Grail setup across time frames: 'When the market breaks out of an extended trading range and makes new momentum highs, there is a sequence that typically unfolds. Price first pulls back to the 20-bar EMA... then the same retracement will occur on the 30-minute chart, then the 60-minute chart, then the 120-minute time frame. By then you should be looking for a top. But each retracement has to be preceded by a 14-bar ADX reading above 30 on that time frame.' Indicator checklist includes 14-period ADX and 20-period EMA; closing breadth (10-period SMA of NYSE advancers minus decliners), TICK/TIKI, and put-call ratio are US internals NOT owned by the Chinese-futures corpus (unavailable-input boundary, not proxied).
